circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Situated on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, the Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke that has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. The circuit represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One venue, following Bahrain's earlier establishment and preceding tracks built in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne that hosts the Formula One Australian Grand Prix each year, alongside the Supercars Championship and additional support categories. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification for motorsport events.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally known as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following a redesign and shortening of the track, it was relaunched under a new name and once again hosted the Austrian Grand Prix during the late 1990s and early 2000s.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street course in Azerbaijan's capital that spans 6. 003 kilometers, ranking it among the longest venues on the Formula One calendar. The track hosted its first F1 race in 2016 as the European Grand Prix, followed by the inaugural Azerbaijan Grand Prix the following year, both organized by the Baku City Circuit Operation Company.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the inaugural Formula One race in the Middle East that same year and continues to annually stage the Bahrain Grand Prix. The FIA Grade 1 licensed facility accommodates various motorsport categories including drag racing, GP2 Series, and endurance racing, while featuring multiple circuit configurations.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, situated in Montmeló near Barcelona, is a 4. 657 km track featuring a balanced layout of extended straights and diverse corner configurations that test driver versatility. With FIA Grade 1 certification and seating for approximately 140,700 spectators, the facility serves as a premier motorsport venue.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: The Belgian circuit at Spa-Francorchamps stretches 7. 004 km through the Walloon region near the town of Spa and has continuously hosted Formula One racing since 1985, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006. This venue has deep roots in Grand Prix history, having staged races since the championship's inaugural 1950 season and maintaining its status as the regular home of the Belgian Grand Prix.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, this 4. 361 km street circuit serves as the permanent home of the Canadian Grand Prix in Formula One. Beyond its primary Formula One role, the venue has hosted various international motorsport series including sports car racing championships and North American racing categories.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this motorsport facility is primarily recognized as the home of the Chinese Grand Prix, which took place annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The venue has expanded its motorsport calendar to include the Shanghai ePrix beginning in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone is a renowned English racing facility situated near Northamptonshire that has served as the traditional venue for Britain's premier motorsport event since 1948. The track gained further significance by hosting the inaugural World Championship race in 1950, though the British Grand Prix subsequently alternated between three venues until establishing a permanent home at Silverstone in 1987. Beyond Formula One, the circuit also functions as a regular stop on the international motorcycle racing calendar.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: Located near Budapest in Mogyoród, the Hungaroring is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix held in Eastern Europe when it opened in 1986. Built in just eight months, faster than any other Formula One venue at the time, the track was constructed outside the city near a highway after plans for a Monaco-style street circuit in Budapest's central park were rejected by the Hungarian government.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit constructed in 1922 that ranks among the world's earliest purpose-built racing venues and the most historic in mainland Europe. The track has hosted the Italian Grand Prix continuously since 1949, excepting a 1980 closure for renovations, making it one of only four circuits to appear on every Formula One calendar since the championship's inception, and its long straights and rapid corners have earned it the nickname "Temple of Speed.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese racing facility situated in Mie Prefecture and operated by Honda Mobilityland. The track, which accommodates 155,000 spectators, has become internationally renowned as a premier venue for Formula One and Super Formula racing.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course navigating through Paradise, Nevada's famous boulevard and its surrounding urban landscape, passing iconic hospitality venues and entertainment landmarks. The track incorporates distinctive Las Vegas locations, creating a racing configuration that showcases the city's most recognizable structures and attractions as integral parts of the circuit layout.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: The Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez in Mexico City is a 4. 304 km circuit named after two Mexican racing brothers who both died in racing accidents, Ricardo in 1962 and Pedro in 1971. The venue has hosted the Formula One Mexican Grand Prix since 2015 on its current layout, resuming a role it previously held during two earlier periods ending in 1992, with the event now officially called the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners and average qualifying speeds approaching 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the Formula One calendar in 2022, the venue primarily hosts the premier motorsport series.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street course that winds through the urban streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, circling the harbour in the Principality of Monaco. Though officially named after the circuit itself, it is widely known simply as "Monte Carlo" due to its location predominantly within that neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, the Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the Dutch Grand Prix after returning to Formula One's schedule in 2021. The venue's partnership with the sport concluded in 2026.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit, situated north of Doha in Qatar, spans 5. 419 kilometers with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight and holds FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km racing circuit in São Paulo, Brazil, originally opened in 1940 and later renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace following his fatal aircraft accident. The counterclockwise track also features a karting facility dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along the Saudi Arabian coastline beside the Red Sea. Since 2021, it has served as the home of the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix, with the facility also hosting Formula E competition beginning in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Marina Bay district, incorporating portions of the Downtown Core and Kallang planning zones into its street course layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, this 4. 657-kilometer facility features a balanced mix of lengthy straights and diverse corner configurations that make it representative of modern racing track design. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that hosts the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside NASCAR, MotoGP, and endurance racing events. The venue has established itself as a major motorsport destination in North America, having previously accommodated various racing series including IndyCar and sports car championships.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai and British driver currently racing for Williams in Formula One, competing under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Fernando Alonso is a Spanish driver currently racing for Aston Martin in Formula One, having secured two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 alongside 32 Grand Prix victories. Beyond single-seaters, he has achieved remarkable success in endurance motorsport, including victories at Le Mans and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both F1 and world-level sportscar titles.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Andrea Kimi Antonelli represents Italy in Formula One, currently driving for Mercedes. The driver has secured eight Grand Prix victories since entering the sport in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Haas, where he competes at the highest level of motorsport.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabi Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One, representing Audi on the grid.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing experience from a 13-season career that includes 10 Grand Prix victories. He previously achieved two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship while competing for Mercedes in 2019 and 2020.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Argentine driver Franco Colapinto currently races in Formula One for the Alpine team. He has established himself as a competitor in the sport's premier racing series.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian motorsport competitor, holds a reserve driver position with Haas while actively racing in the European Le Mans Series' LMP2 category with Nielsen Racing. He has participated in seven Formula One grands prix during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly, a French driver, currently races for Alpine in Formula One. The highlight of his career came when he achieved victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Hadjar represents France in Formula One while competing for Red Bull Racing, though he holds dual French and Algerian citizenship.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari, holding a joint-record seven world championship titles alongside Michael Schumacher. The driver also leads in multiple statistical categories, including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: Nicolas Hülkenberg is a German Formula One driver currently racing for Audi. Beyond his single-seater commitments, he achieved endurance racing success by winning the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 with Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Monégasque driver Charles Leclerc currently races for Ferrari in Formula One, having secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his career. He achieved his best championship result as runner-up in 2022, competing for the same Maranello-based team.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Danish driver Kevin Magnussen competed in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014 to 2020 and again from 2022 to 2024. He currently focuses on endurance racing with BMW at WRT in the FIA World Endurance Championship while also pursuing a part-time NASCAR career with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver currently racing for McLaren, secured the Formula One World Drivers' Championship in 2025 and has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The driver previously achieved his sole grand prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while competing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: The Mexican driver competes for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from 15 seasons in the sport. Pérez finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull and has secured six Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: An Australian driver competing in Formula One for McLaren, Oscar Piastri has claimed victory in nine Grand Prix races throughout his four seasons in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo is an Australian driver who competed in the sport's top racing series for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight race victories during his career. Known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," he concluded his Formula One involvement in 2024.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell represents Britain in Formula One, currently racing for Mercedes, where he has accumulated eight Grand Prix victories over his eight seasons in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes in Formula One for Williams and has achieved four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American racing driver who competed in Formula One during the 2023-2024 seasons. He currently races in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category for Proton Competition, having previously participated in IMSA's LMP2 class with Era Motorsport.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin, bringing his competitive skills to one of the sport's established teams.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Japanese driver Yuki Tsunoda held a full-time Formula One seat from 2021 through 2025 before transitioning to a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: A Dutch-Belgian driver competing for Red Bull Racing, Max Verstappen has claimed four consecutive Formula One World Drivers' Championship titles between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12 seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, China's sole Formula One competitor to date, raced in the championship from 2022 through 2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with Cadillac. He currently holds a development position with the American team while maintaining his status as the only driver from his nation to have participated in the sport's highest level.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has raced under the Alpine banner since 2021, when Renault rebranded its works operation to showcase its Alpine sports car marque. Following Renault's factory withdrawal at the conclusion of 2025, the squad transitioned from being a manufacturer-backed outfit to an independent competitor.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has competed in Formula One through different organizational structures, with the current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited and competing under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari represents the racing operations of Italian luxury automobile manufacturer Ferrari and serves as one of Formula One's most decorated competitors. As the sport's oldest continuously competing team since the inaugural 1950 championship, Ferrari has established itself as the most successful outfit in the discipline's history, earning widespread recognition through their iconic emblem nickname.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: TGR Haas F1 Team is an American-licensed outfit founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas that entered Formula One in 2016. Led by team principal Ayao Komatsu since January 2024, the organization replaced Guenther Steiner, who held the position from the team's establishment through its early competitive years.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss engineering and racing enterprise established by Peter Sauber in 1970, the organization first distinguished itself in endurance competition before joining Formula One in 1993 as an independent manufacturer. The team competed continuously for over three decades until its exit in 2025, becoming one of the championship's longest-tenured constructors, before Audi acquired its operations to launch its own works effort.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that competes under the McLaren Mastercard banner. The team operates as part of the McLaren Group, with ultimate ownership residing with Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 as both constructor and power unit supplier. The current team, registered under a German licence and headquartered in Brackley, operates as Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team, with ownership shared equally among Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff since 2022. The marque is traditionally associated with the "Silver Arrows" nomenclature.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024, operating as one of two Red Bull-owned squads alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with a supporting facility in Milton Keynes, the team represents Red Bull GmbH's dual-team structure in the sport.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024 as one of two Red Bull-owned squads, alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with operations in Milton Keynes, the team operates as a second outfit within the Austrian conglomerate's motorsport portfolio.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team based in England, owned by Red Bull GmbH alongside Racing Bulls. Founded in 2005 under the long-standing leadership of Christian Horner, the team transitioned to new management under Laurent Mekies in 2025.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head following the collapse of Williams's previous F1 venture, is a British constructor competing as Atlassian Williams F1 Team in 2026. Headquartered on a substantial facility in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team has established itself as a significant presence in Formula One since its inception.
